resources.string: A research activity is available. Unlock your phone to see it.
A quiet daily reminder that the study is collecting or paused
Shown while a consented research study is collecting data
Particeps is running a research study.
Still collecting. Open the app to pause, export, or withdraw.
Paused since %1$s. Nothing is being collected until you resume.
Paused. Nothing is being collected until you resume.
A submitted response is final. You can review it, but you cannot change or submit it again.
Submitted. This response is now read-only.
This survey occurrence has expired and cannot be submitted.
Complete the required questions and check each answer.
Checking recorded study data. A study that has been collecting for a while can take longer here.
Connect to the internet and scan your researcher’s QR code. Review the study before deciding to join.
When Particeps’ own screens open, move to the foreground or background, and close, and which Particeps screen it was.
activity in other apps, or what is shown on Particeps’ screens
Raw acceleration of the phone along three axes, including gravity, with each reading’s sensor time and accuracy.
audio, images, or location; no activity such as walking is inferred
Whole battery percentage, charging state, charging source, and whether power-saving mode is on.
battery health, temperature, or hardware identity
The phone’s time-zone setting, UTC offset, and daylight-saving state, and why each was recorded, such as the study starting or the time zone or clock changing.
location; the time zone is a phone setting and no travel is inferred from it
Raw rotation speed of the phone around three axes, with each reading’s sensor time and accuracy.
audio, images, or location; no orientation or activity is inferred
The light level measured by the phone’s light sensor, with each reading’s sensor time and accuracy.
images, or anything about your surroundings beyond the light level
Whether something is close to the phone’s proximity sensor, the raw distance reading, the sensor’s range, and the sensor time.
images or who is nearby; a near reading does not mean a person is present, and many phones report only near or far
Whether the screen is on, off, or in a low-power display mode, whether the phone is interactive, and whether the lock screen is showing.
what is on the screen; a screen that is on does not show that you are looking at it or using the phone

Whether the phone’s main connection is available and whether it uses Wi-Fi, mobile data, ethernet, or a VPN; whether it is metered or roaming; and whether Android confirmed that it reaches the internet. It may include Android’s estimate of the connection’s speed.
network names, addresses, websites, or the content of your traffic
Whether any VPN on this phone is connected, including VPNs from other apps, as Android reports it.
which VPN app it is, VPN server addresses, or the content of your traffic
How many bytes the whole phone sent and received in each measured interval, and when each interval began and ended.
which app used the data, destinations, or content; no speed test is run
Total bytes and packets the whole phone sent and received over Wi-Fi or mobile data, for each period Android reports.
which app used the data, destinations, or content

When apps come to the foreground and leave it, with each app’s package name when Android provides it and a code that tells an app’s screens apart without naming them; when the screen turns on or off; when the lock screen appears or is dismissed; and when the phone starts up or shuts down.
what is shown on the screen, what you type, notification content, or the names of an app’s screens

The phone’s location (latitude and longitude) with its accuracy and time, including while Particeps is not open. It may include altitude, speed, and direction of travel with their accuracy, and whether Android marked the location as simulated.
photos, nearby-device scans, or place names; Particeps does not infer which places you visit

For touches on the Particeps research keyboard only: the kind of key (letter, space, backspace, or enter), where on the key and when you touched it, and the touch pressure, size, and angle as the phone reports them.
which letter you pressed, the text you type, touches in password fields, or input from any other keyboard
Check this against the fingerprint your research team published.
A signature shows the file has not been altered since it was signed. It does not show who wrote it.
This configuration contains no researcher-assigned participant code.
Check this opaque code against the one the research team gave you. The app does not ask for your name, email, or phone number.
This import also gets a separate random installation code. It links this installation’s encrypted chunks and distinguishes repeated imports.
This study does not send data automatically
What it collects stays on this phone until you export it yourself.
Only the research team\'s key can open what is sent. Neither the network it travels over nor the server that receives it can read the contents.
A randomly generated code travels with the data so the team can tell participants apart. It contains no name and no account.

Automatic sending is part of this study and cannot be switched off on its own. Pausing or withdrawing stops new collection, but data already collected and not yet sent can still be sent to the research team.
I have read and agree to the data collection and sharing described above.
Study status and ongoing collection; scheduled activities when configured
The study keeps running. Restore any item below to resume only the optional sources that use it.
This phone does not provide this sensor. There is no setting or substitute that can enable it.
Android reports that this phone cannot satisfy the location settings required by this study. Contact the research team before starting.
Particeps could not verify whether this phone can satisfy the study’s configured location request. Contact the research team before starting.
This phone does not provide the required Android settings screen. Contact the research team before starting.

This study may use a VPN on this device to adjust how quickly apps on this phone transfer data. Traffic stays on your usual network and is not sent through a Particeps server, and Particeps does not record its content or destinations. Particeps may check whether particular apps are installed, but it does not save or upload a list of your installed apps. On Android 17 or later, local-network access is used only to forward local connections that apps start; Particeps does not look for devices on your local network. Another VPN can interrupt this function; if that happens, the study pauses.
Android no longer offers the permission dialog after repeated denial. Restore precise location from Particeps App info.
In App info, open Permissions, then Location.
Choose Allow only while using the app and turn on Use precise location.
Return to Particeps; it checks the real Android setting automatically.
Android must be able to satisfy this study’s exact location request, including its configured accuracy and update settings.
Turn on Use location and the location-accuracy services required by this study.
Return to Particeps; it checks the exact configured location request automatically.
For continuous location collection, Android requires a separate setting. This study may collect location in the background while Particeps is closed or not in use.
In App info, open Permissions, then Location.
Return to Particeps; it checks the real Android setting automatically.
Android settings are required when the permission dialog can no longer grant access or a required Particeps notification channel is off.
Keep Active research collection and Daily study reminder enabled. If this study has scheduled activities, keep Research activities enabled too.
Return to Particeps; it checks the permission and required channels automatically.
Android treats app and network usage as special access, so a normal permission dialog cannot enable it.
Find and open Particeps on the Usage access screen.
Return to Particeps; it checks the real Android setting automatically.
The research keyboard is an Android input method and must be enabled in system settings before it can be selected.
Enable Research keyboard and confirm Android’s warning.
Return to Particeps after the keyboard is enabled.
After enabling the research keyboard, choose it as the current keyboard in Android’s picker.
Choose Research keyboard in the system keyboard picker.
Return to Particeps; it checks the selected keyboard automatically.
Some data that was already sent has been removed from this phone. A later export will not include it.
Reread what you agreed to, what is collected, and your choices
Particeps also uses notifications for study status and ongoing collection, and for scheduled activities when a study has them.
Confirmed once Particeps can verify the phone’s clock

Pause stops every data category until you choose Resume. While the study is paused, Particeps still records when the phone’s clock or time zone changes, including the new time zone, and when the phone restarts, so that the study’s timeline stays correct. Resume checks the required Android access again.
Data that was already collected continues to be sent while the study is paused.
Withdrawing ends collection permanently. You do not need to give a reason, and you can still export what was already collected.
Data already collected but not yet sent may still be sent to the research team.

After the study is completed or withdrawn, Delete local data removes the study and everything it recorded from this phone. This cannot be undone, so export first if the research team should receive a copy.

Deleting also cancels any sending that has not happened yet. Data already sent cannot be deleted from this phone. To ask the research team about it, you need the researcher’s contact details and your installation code shown above; deleting removes both from this phone, so note them first.
Collection will stop permanently. You can still export what was already collected.
All collection stops permanently. You can still export what was already collected, until you delete it.

Collection has not started, so none of the data this study asks for has been collected, and no study data has been sent to the research team. Declining removes the study and your setup progress from this phone. This cannot be undone. Android access you granted during setup stays on until you turn it off in Android Settings or uninstall Particeps.

Collection has not started, so none of the data this study asks for has been collected. An earlier version of Particeps already sent records of your setup steps, such as when you accepted the consent, and your installation code to the research team; declining does not take them back. Declining removes the study and your setup progress from this phone. This cannot be undone. Android access you granted during setup stays on until you turn it off in Android Settings or uninstall Particeps.

Encrypted events, study state, and the configuration are all removed, including the researcher’s contact details and your installation code. If you may later ask the research team about data already sent or exported, write both down from Study and my data first. This cannot be undone.
Important actions needed to safely restore research collection.
Open Particeps to safely restore collection.
Particeps could not finish automatic recovery. Fix any requested Android access, then try again.
Delete old study data and restart?

This permanently deletes the existing study instance and all data that has not been exported. If the configuration is still valid, you will review consent and permissions again with a new installation code and a full study duration. This cannot be undone.
Particeps could not open that study configuration.
The study could not be loaded. Check your internet connection and scan again, or contact your researcher.
Particeps could not export the study data.
Particeps could not check the required Android access.
Particeps could not complete that action.
Particeps could not reset the local study.
Particeps could not delete the local study data.
The encrypted study export is ready.
Choose where to save the export.
Stopping the export and removing the unfinished file. This may take a moment.
Try exporting again. If it still fails, contact your researcher.
The unfinished file could not be removed. Check the location you chose and delete it.
Finish or cancel the export before deleting local data.
The local study data was deleted.
The study was removed from this phone.
The study paused because Particeps could not verify safe collection. Review any Android access shown below, then resume.
